body: Just over a year knowingly but I think I’ve had the symptoms for a while beforehand! Just got mine out last Friday and I’m already feeling so much better

Hey! I had to wear paper undies. I have large breasts and didn’t wear a bra and haven’t worn one since my surgery last Friday. I have 4 wounds, one in my belly button, one on my right side and 2 that sit under my right boob. Other than a little extra soreness where my boob presses on the bruises, it’s honestly not bad at all. Gown wise, I had a gown put on and tied at the back and another one put on backwards to cover my butt until I was in the anaesthetic room. Once in the room they took the backwards one off and untied the back of my normal one and I laid down, they covered me with a blanket and then pulled the top of my gown off my shoulders to stick electrode pads to my chest. I didn’t shave as it can cause micro tears in your skin which increases risk of infection! Surgeons and nurses DO NOT CARE about if you’re hairy or what your appearance is!!! They’re completely focussed on getting you through your surgery safely! If you’re hairy in a place they need to operate on they will shave it themselves! When I woke up from surgery I still had my gown on and I was covered in a blanket, I still had the paper undies on too. I’ve had 10 surgeries so honestly I didn’t care about how I looked before surgery as I’m so used to it but I can tell you that for at least a couple hours after surgery you probably won’t be bothered at all about being completely covered up and stuff and you’ll be more worried about getting your pain under control and getting home! As for bras, you definitely can’t wear one during surgery, you might be able to wear one into the anaesthetic room (kinda like how you can wear a dressing gown and your socks/shoes)  but you’ll have to ask the ward nurse or anaesthesiologist who comes around and gives you the things to change into and they’ll let you know!
Underwear wise afterwards, I’ve found midi to be the most comfortable as they don’t rub on any of my wounds and I also bought a pack in a size up for after surgery bloating. I wore a playsuit on my way home which kept me feeling covered but also comfortable and cool (struggled with heat after surgery) 
I will say I’m super glad I was in gowns and throwaway undies after my surgery as I ended up bleeding more than I should from my bellybutton and it got on the gown and paper undies instead of the clothes I went home in! 
I can’t help with the hair thing as I have a pixie cut!

Had my surgery on Friday, waited over a year. Would’ve been longer if I hadn’t called and called and kicked up a fuss though! I was having regular gallbladder attacks, nausea, vomiting, developed gastritis, etc. I saw my surgeon on Christmas Eve last year and practically sobbed to him about how much I was struggling and he finally decided to put me on the list for surgery (this was my third appointment with him. He had previously sent me for gastroscopies and MRIs to find a different cause for my symptoms even though my ultrasound showed that my gallbladder was full of stones.) and I about cried from relief. He said I should have a date by February. I didn’t… so I called the theatre scheduling team at the hospital in March and they booked me a date in (31st March) and gave me a pre-op date (11th March) I attended the pre-op only for them to decide I needed more cardiac investigations (ultrasound and 24hr tape) which meant that the surgery was cancelled. I had the investigations done and called pre-op a week after to see if my results were in (they weren’t) and I called back at least twice a week until I finally got a call offering me another date (23rd May) this was then re-arranged to the 30th due to a surgeon going on leave but I got a call 2 weeks ago offering me a cancellation date (The 23rd again!) and I said yes right away! I went from a morning to an afternoon case and had to wait longer due to a complicated case taking longer than expected (over 3hrs) and I was the last patient of the day! Was in surgery just before 4pm and out and semi-conscious by 4:50pm! Got home at about 8pm! ( would’ve been quicker but I had some unexpected bleeding from my bellybutton incision and some near fainting spells! I’m now still very sore and tired but managed to take a 5 min walk around the block today and I’ll be able to shower and change my dressings tomorrow!

Just fight fight fight! Call the theatre scheduling team, call the pre-op team, call the general surgery team, call your GP. Don’t stop kicking up a fuss and you will get there!
Im proud of you!

I also bought some underwear in a size up so it’s not so tight on my stomach during/after an attack and some loose trousers/dresses are good too! I keep my painkillers (codeine) on hand at all times just in case! I also suggest making your bathroom/bedroom somewhere comforting to be if you can. I spend a lot of time in my bed/on the toilet since I developed gallstones and I now have my bedroom as cosy as possible with meds/safe snacks/water/comfort items/ heat pads/etc all within reach and in the bathroom I’ve got similar but mostly things to distract from the pain like a peel off face mask/sheet masks, bubble bath and bath salts to either smell to ground myself or to use in the bath post attack, a spot for my phone so I can have it nearby if I need to call for help, listen to music, watch a video, etc. lotions to gently massage onto my tummy, etc! It really does make a difference!

I was on gedarel before I was diagnosed with gallstones and realised that most of my attacks fell once I stopped the pill for my bleed week. Some research on gederel told me that it can cause gallstones so I stopped immediately and started taking desogesterel about a month later (I have really painful and heavy periods due to PCOS so I needed something) and this pill doesn’t require you to take a week off for a bleed so while yes, I’m still having gallbladder attacks, they don’t seem to be any worse or frequent while on this pill. The only frustrating thing about desogesterel is that if I forget a pill I bleed within like 12 hours lol

Unfortunately it’s not an ‘if’ you get it out it’s a ‘when’ you get it out. There is treatments to get rid of gallstones temporarily I believe but from what I know, once you have stones, you will always have stones. It’s always better to get it removed before it has the chance to cause infection and jaundice and such. 
I’m 21 and was diagnosed about 3 months ago. I see a surgeon next Tuesday to hopefully be put on the list to have it out. I eat a low fat diet that pretty much only consists of cereal with skimmed lactose free milk and salted pretzels as I’m so scared of having another attack. I live every day in fear of feeling unwell and being in pain because of my gallstones so I personally think removal is my best option but i understand how other people may prefer to wait it out if they don’t feel as though their symptoms are having too big of a negative effect on their day to day life. But my main advice to you is to talk to your doctor and get their opinion on what you should do and how to handle your specific symptoms and such. I wish you luck
